top.headline: The Trump Administration Quietly Subpoenaed a National Teachers Union Over Pro-Palestine Student Activists
top.blurb: A federal grand jury subpoena, obtained exclusively by The Intercept, seeks the American Federation of Teachers' membership rolls and meeting minutes going back to 2023, part of a probe into University of Michigan protesters now facing felony charges. The union's campus local is fighting to quash a similar subpoena, calling it an attempt to criminalize labor organizing alongside student dissent.

top.headline: A New HUD Rule Would Force Mixed-Status Families to Choose Between Separation and Eviction
top.blurb: A final HUD rule taking effect in mid-December will cut off federal housing assistance to households where any member is undocumented, an estimated 80,000 people including 37,000 children. U.S. citizens in those households face new verification burdens too, and HUD's own analysis puts the added cost at roughly $300 million even as the agency does less on homelessness broadly.

top.headline: An Oklahoma Senator Who Used to Run a Pipeline Company Is Writing the Rules That Could Revive One
top.blurb: Sen. Alan Armstrong, appointed rather than elected, still holds stock in Williams Companies, the pipeline firm he used to run, and he's pushing a permitting bill that would strip states of power to block pipelines like Williams' long-dead Constitution project. Former Williams colleagues staff his office; one kept his old job while serving as his chief of staff.

top.headline: India's First Post-SIR Voter Rolls Show Gains Up to 3% — and Seven States Still Unaccounted For
top.blurb: The Election Commission's first draft rolls since the contentious Special Intensive Revision show voter counts rising 0.1%-3% in nine states, with Kerala and Tamil Nadu still below pre-SIR levels. Two of the Commission's own members have objected 14 times to how the revision was run.

top.headline: Ladakh Activist Sonam Wangchuk Says Police Confined Him to His Home Ahead of Local Polls
top.blurb: Sonam Wangchuk says he's been barred from leaving home under a 60-day prohibitory order after questioning why a probe into September 2025's deadly Leh protest is stalled and why hill council polls are set for midwinter. He plans to challenge the order in court.

top.headline: Iran Claims Its First Strike on a US Military Target in a Gulf Country Since September
top.blurb: Iran's Revolutionary Guard says it destroyed a US early-warning radar installation in Bahrain, calling it retaliation for an earlier strike on a telecoms tower in Iran's Hormozgan province. Washington and Manama had not responded by publication, and the IRGC cast the strike as a warning over Strait of Hormuz oil smuggling and what it calls aerial provocations.

top.headline: As Finland Detects a Strike on a Russian Warship, Kushner and Witkoff Shuttle Between Moscow and Zelenskyy
top.blurb: Finland's military detected a rare strike on a Russian navy vessel in the Gulf of Finland, which Ukraine's security service claimed credit for, even as US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff met Putin in Moscow and then Zelenskyy in Ireland. The shuttle diplomacy follows UAE talks that produced a prisoner swap but no real breakthrough.

top.headline: Two Jihadist Factions Are Killing Each Other in Burkina Faso, and No One's Sure That's Good News
top.blurb: JNIM and its rival ISSP have fought increasingly deadly battles along Burkina Faso's border with Mali since September, with more than 2,200 fighters killed in their rivalry since 2019, per ACLED. Analysts say the infighting may drain JNIM's resources, but it offers little relief for a population caught in a worsening humanitarian crisis as the state loses ground.

top.headline: Australian Debutant Mahli Beardman Takes 6/24 to Rout England in Perth ODI
top.blurb: Mahli Beardman, 21, took 6/24 on his ODI debut as England collapsed to 131 all out in the first ODI in Perth, dismissing captain Harry Brook and Joe Root inside the first 14 overs. It's the best-ever ODI debut bowling figures by an Australian man, and only the second five-wicket debut haul by an Australian in the format's history, after Tony Dodemaide's in 1988.

top.headline: Four Lopsided Chases Open the ICC Women's Emerging Nations Trophy in the UAE
top.blurb: Sri Lanka, Scotland, Pakistan and the Netherlands all won big on the opening day of the Emerging Nations Trophy in the UAE, with Sri Lanka chasing down Ireland's total for a 10-wicket win inside 13 overs. The event gives associate and developing women's sides rare multi-match exposure outside the main international calendar.

top.headline: 'I Play Rocky' Review: A Salute to Stallone's Persistence, and a Love Letter to Hollywood
top.blurb: Nandini Ramnath reviews Peter Farrelly's dramatized account of how a struggling Sylvester Stallone fought to write and star in 'Rocky.' She finds it crisp, well-played and full of fun Hollywood in-jokes, but ultimately a nostalgic crowd-pleaser that avoids any real darkness about the industry it celebrates.

bengal.headline: A Job Candidate's EWS Certificate Was Denied Because His Parent's Name Vanished in the SIR Purge
bengal.blurb: Calcutta High Court fast-tracked a challenge from a recruitment candidate whose economically-weaker-section certificate was withheld only because his parent's name had been struck from the electoral rolls during the SIR revision.

bengal.headline: Calcutta High Court Won't Order an Inquiry Into Who Tore Down a Civil Liberties Group's Book Stall
bengal.blurb: The court dismissed a civil-rights group's plea for an independent probe into the demolition of its unauthorised book stall, ruling that no fundamental right had clearly been violated, and left the question of who ordered it unanswered.

travel.headline: A December Guide to New York Skips Midtown's Crowds for Dyker Heights' Dazzling Brooklyn Lights
travel.blurb: Lonely Planet's holiday guide steers visitors away from Fifth Avenue's Thanksgiving-to-New Year's crowds toward Dyker Heights, the Brooklyn neighborhood famous for its over-the-top Christmas light displays.

travel.headline: Jaguars Are Supposed to Be Loners. In Brazil's Pantanal, They Play, Groom and Hunt Together.
travel.blurb: A 13-year study of 459 Pantanal jaguars recorded 167 pair encounters, nearly 39% of them social rather than hostile, challenging the cat's reputation as a strict solitary hunter.

happy.headline: The Real Victorian Surgeon Who Diagnosed Strangers by Their Shoes — and Became Sherlock Holmes
happy.blurb: Edinburgh surgeon Joseph Bell spotted a deserter's hidden tattoo, diagnosed alcoholism from a hidden whiskey bottle, and guessed strangers' lives on train platforms, astonishing his student Arthur Conan Doyle, who turned him into Sherlock Holmes.

tech_top.headline: Nvidia's Jensen Huang Resigns as CEO After Affair Scandal, Erasing $855 Billion in Market Value
tech_top.blurb: Nvidia's board accepted Huang's resignation days after he admitted to an affair with an alleged Chinese spy. CFO Colette Kress becomes interim CEO; shares have fallen nearly 19% since Friday, and the company reports earnings Tuesday without him for the first time in its history.
tech_top.pm_note: A company this large had no visible succession plan for a 33-year founder-CEO — a reminder that even product org charts need a named backup two levels deep, not just at the top.

tech_top.headline: Democrats Open Nvidia Inquiry, Alleging Trump Traded China Chip Access for Political Favors
tech_top.blurb: Two Democratic lawmakers allege Trump let Nvidia sell H200 chips to China in exchange for a tariff functioning as an export tax, then let the Huang scandal play out quietly. It's the second congressional probe into the chipmaker this week, after a Republican-led group requested Huang's testimony.
tech_top.pm_note: Export licensing isn't a back-office compliance checkbox: it can become the center of a political scandal that moves your stock double digits in a morning.

tech_more.headline: A Second Breach at Fireworks AI Exposed Notion Customers' AI Chat Transcripts
tech_more.blurb: Hackers breached AI infrastructure provider Fireworks AI for the second time in two months, reaching Notion's AI chat transcripts for about 1% of its customers before Notion cut the connection.

tech_101.text: US government permission required before certain advanced technology, like Nvidia's AI chips, can be sold to specific foreign buyers, meant to keep sensitive tech out of rivals' hands.
Software that acts on your behalf, booking a flight or managing an account, without a human clicking each step, which is exactly what's making banks and airlines nervous about fraud.

science.headline: A Reusable 'Molecular Fabric' Could End One of Chemistry's Most Energy-Hungry Jobs
science.blurb: A self-assembling, woven fabric built from interlocking molecular networks pulled about 98% of the benzene out of a benzene-cyclohexane mixture, chemicals nearly impossible to separate by distillation because they boil at almost the same temperature. The fabric can be heated and reused, aimed at one of industry's biggest energy sinks.

science.headline: Perseverance Finds Organic Carbon Just Beneath the Surface of an Ancient Mars Lakebed
science.blurb: NASA's rover detected complex organic carbon a few microns deep in Jezero Crater mudstone, the shallowest such find yet on Mars. It doesn't prove ancient life, since non-biological chemistry can also produce organics, but it shows carbon-based material was widespread across the planet's ancient surface.

science.headline: A Magnetism Breakthrough Could Let AI Chips Run on Far Less Power
science.blurb: Brown University engineers grew ultrathin films of a 'multiferroic' material that keep their electrical and magnetic properties at a few atoms thick, avoiding a defect that normally kills such effects when shrunk. The films unexpectedly also showed a fast, compact magnetic state that could underpin low-power memory and logic chips.

philosophy.headline: A Good Sceptic Has More Than Doubt and Less Than Certainty
philosophy.blurb: Philosopher Massimo Pigliucci revives Cicero's Academic Scepticism: beliefs strong enough to act on but never certain, always open to revision. He contrasts this with climate-denying 'scepticism' on one side and certainty-demanding scientism on the other, and offers it as a working method for science, politics and daily life.

philosophy.headline: Habermas's Theory of Truth Meant He Changed His Mind
philosophy.blurb: Emilie Prattico traces how Jürgen Habermas abandoned his own earlier claim that truth is just what people would agree to under fair conditions, once he recognized facts answer to the world while moral claims answer only to discourse, a distinction she argues matters more as social media fragments public debate.

philosophy_101.text: Cicero's idea that you can hold a belief strongly enough to act on it without claiming certainty, and should drop it the moment better evidence shows up.
The idea that political decisions are legitimate when they come from open, reasoned debate among citizens, not just from counting votes.
